subject: URGENT: OrangeField production degradation — request for temporary capacity prioritization
messages:
From: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@orangefield.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — suspected throttling (OrangeField)

Ben —

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and token throttling on our inference endpoints around 02:00 UTC this morning. This is affecting live traffic for our personalization feature and a press demo scheduled for tomorrow. The attached impact report has error traces and sample request IDs.

We believe the requests are being queued or dropped at the GPU routing layer — latency goes from ~120ms to 1.2s and tokens/sec drops by ~60%. Our legal/comms team is breathing down our neck because of the demo. Can Redwood temporarily prioritize our production lane until we ship the next model rollout (target: 72 hours)? We are prepared to sign a short-term committed addendum or convert more capacity into a reserved tranche if that helps.

Please advise urgently.

Thanks,
Sofia Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering
OrangeField AI

Attachments:
- OrangeField_impact_report.pdf (pdf, 87KB)
- DF-4821_SOW_v3.docx (docx, 42KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Production latency spike — suspected throttling (OrangeField)

Team — forwarding an urgent escalation from OrangeField (DF-4821). Key points: they are seeing ~60% token throughput degradation, customer is on a mid-tier Dedicated commitment with monthly burst credits. Demo tomorrow is time-sensitive.

Options I see (please weigh in quickly):
- Quick path: bump OrangeField to Priority-1 for the next 48–72 hours by reallocating up to 20% of our burst pool from non-critical tenants (temporary, reversible).
- Conservative path: schedule a phased slot swap — shift some reserved capacity from low-usage tranches, requires coordination and 6–8 hour window for rolling jobs and public notice.

This is a revenue-risk / upsell opportunity: if we can stabilize them for the demo and they convert to a larger Dedicated commitment, we lock the deal (DF-4821). Need a TA on technical feasibility and a ruling from allocations policy (Laura) and sales leadership (Marissa) by 11:45 PST.

Ben
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Production latency spike — suspected throttling (OrangeField)

Ben —

I dug into the router and pool metrics for the last 24h. Summary: OrangeField is hitting a long-tail of contexts causing inefficient KV-cache pressure (model size + long histories). Router is not dropping requests; it is falling back to a lower-throughput execution path when the preferred pool is saturated. Current committed Dedicated pool occupancy: 82%. Burst pool headroom: ~18%. We can do a temporary reallocation but there are trade-offs.

Two technically viable actions (fast):
A) Immediate burst shift (recommended minimal risk): Elevate OrangeField traffic by 15% of burst capacity for 48 hours. Impact: expected to restore ~40–50% of lost throughput for them, negligible impact for most burst consumers. Risk: may increase latency on extremely bursty, non-critical customers; no SLA breach expected.

B) Reserve tranche borrowing (higher impact): Move 1 reserved node from low-utilization tranche X-764 (customer: BrightSketch) into OrangeField's pool for 72 hours. Impact: likely full restoration for OrangeField demo, but risks an SLA exception for BrightSketch unless we pre-notify and migrate their jobs. Operational complexity: ~6h rolling change, requires allocation approval.

If neither option is acceptable we can instead apply a model-level mitigation: temporarily reduce max_batch_size for contexts flagged in the report — moderate improvement, minimal infra change, but less reliable.

I need a firm direction by 12:00 PST to enact A or begin the migration for B. If we go with B, coordinate with LAURA and Ops runbook RB-4.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Quoted: 
> "We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency ..." — Sofia (OrangeField)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Production latency spike — suspected throttling (OrangeField)

Ben / Karthik —

Sales POV: We should prioritize OrangeField for the immediate window. They've been signaling willingness to convert to a larger reserved tranche and legal is already reviewing the SOW addendum (attached). The revenue upside and the PR risk of a failed demo justify a short conservative commitment on our side. Proposed decision:

1) Approve Karthik's option A immediately (15% burst shift for 48 hours).
2) Parallel motion: Ben, work with finance to push a quick addendum for a 6-month upfront committed tranche. Offer a temporary credit to smooth transition (up to one week of burst refunds) if they sign within 5 business days.
3) Laura, draft an exception memo documenting the temporary tranche reallocation and the rollback trigger. We want traceability and a rollback window of T+72h.

I do not want us to touch reserved nodes from other paying customers without explicit consent (i.e., avoid option B unless BrightSketch signs off). Option A is a good compromise: fast, reversible, and protects our SLAs broadly.

Marissa
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

P.S. Ben — please confirm that the customer accepts the temporary prioritization and the commercial ask (commitment timeline). I'll loop Legal if we need an emergency amendment.
